title: Pick the decoder from the Content-Encoding header

blocks.text: Sensors upload their readings to the ingest API, some compressed. `BodyDecoder` looks at the request's `Content-Encoding` header and wraps the body in the matching decoder. The API accepts `identity`, `gzip` (and its old alias `x-gzip`) and `deflate`. The firmware of one vendor sends `GZIP`, an older gateway sends no `Content-Encoding` header at all for uncompressed bodies, and the service is about to be deployed to a data centre in Istanbul whose servers run with a Turkish default locale.

Write `codecFor(String contentEncoding)` in `src/main/java/practice/BodyDecoder.java` with a `switch` statement, so every one of those clients is understood, and an encoding the API doesn't accept is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: gzip, x-gzip, deflate and identity, written in lower case, pick their codec
a gzip-compressed upload is decoded to its original text
an encoding the API doesn't accept is refused with IllegalArgumentException
an encoding written with capitals picks the same codec as in lower case
a request without the header is read as it is, with no exception
a capitalised encoding is understood on a server whose default locale is Turkish

origin.section: A null Selector Throws Before Any Label Is Compared, default Included

concepts: A protocol value normalised with toLowerCase() depends on the default locale (a Turkish I lowers to a dotless i); toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) doesn't.
A null selector throws NullPointerException before any label is compared, so a default doesn't catch it; the code checks for null first or uses case null.
A switch on a String matches with hashCode and equals: a value built at run time matches its literal, and the match is exact and case-sensitive.
